summary.text: Brian Bengs is a retired U.S. Air Force lieutenant colonel and judge advocate officer, attorney and former Northern State University criminal justice professor. He was the Democratic nominee for this seat in 2022, losing to John Thune, and is running in 2026 as an independent. He says he is campaigning on getting money out of politics and lowering the cost of living.

paragraphs.text: Is an enlisted U.S. Navy veteran and a retired U.S. Air Force officer (lieutenant colonel), and has lived and worked in the United States and abroad.

Earned a bachelor's degree in history and international studies from Iowa State University (1994), a J.D. from the University of Iowa (1996), a master's degree in history from Louisiana Tech University (2007), and a master's degree in international and comparative law from George Washington University (2007).
Served as an Air Force judge advocate general (JAG) officer, including as chief of general law/assistant general counsel for the Air Force.

Taught law and policy topics at the U.S. Air Force Academy, the International Institute of Humanitarian Law, the NATO School Oberammergau and Northern State University, where he was an assistant professor and criminal justice professor.
Later worked as a Wind Cave National Park ranger, according to his April 2025 campaign announcement.
Was the Democratic nominee for this U.S. Senate seat in 2022, losing to John Thune 69.6% to 26.1%.

Announced on April 30, 2025 that he would run as an independent in 2026; Ballotpedia lists the Democratic primary winner, Julian Beaudion, as withdrawn. Bengs describes himself as a husband and father and says he has been active in South Dakota civic activities.
